item.title: The square achievement game on $n \times n$ boards
item.description: arXiv:2610.22410v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two players alternately claim cells of an $n \times n$ grid; the first to hold all four corners of an axis-parallel square wins, and a full board without one is a draw. The first player has a winning strategy if and only if $n \ge 5$, which answers a question of Erickson. For $n \ge 6$ one strategy serves every board: a rule with no lookup table whose moves after the second reply are all forcing, built around the plus, a stone with the four cells at a common distance from it along the axes, a shape proposed for this game by Sirgedas in 2010. The rule is checked on the boards of size $6$ to $17$, and a simulation theorem carries one checked run on the $23 \times 23$ board to every larger board. The proofs are formalized in Lean 4, and the theorem for the rule states that the tree of its own moves is winning.
item.dc:creator: Sean Reid

item.title: Generating functions of hypermaps and m-constellations with two alternating boundaries
item.description: arXiv:2610.22493v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the enumeration of planar hypermaps with several alternating boundaries. We first derive a peeling recursion with an arbitrary number of alternating boundaries and, in the two- boundary case, translate it into a functional equation for the corresponding generating function. Our main result is an explicit solution of this equation for m-constellations. In particular, we obtain a rational expression for the genus-zero two-point function, or cylinder generating function, with two alternating boundaries.
item.dc:creator: Chebasov Dmitry

item.title: Asymptotic dimension of graphs excluding an induced or fat minor
item.description: arXiv:2610.22495v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Asymptotic dimension is a large-scale invariant of metric spaces that was introduced by Gromov (1993). A major open problem in coarse graph theory asks whether, for every fixed graph $H$, the class of graphs excluding $H$ as a fat minor has bounded asymptotic dimension. A weaker conjecture asserts the same conclusion for graphs excluding $H$ as an induced minor. We substantially expand the range of graphs $H$ for which these conjectures are known to hold. Specifically, we prove bounded asymptotic dimension for the following classes of graphs: graphs excluding a fixed planar graph as a fat minor; and graphs excluding a fixed string graph as an induced minor. All of our results also hold for the stronger notion of Assouad--Nagata dimension, a refinement of asymptotic dimension. These results have a number of applications, two of which we mention here. First they imply that an induced minor-closed class is $\chi$-bounded if and only if it does not contain some Burling graph. Second they imply that, in graph classes excluding a fixed planar graph as an induced minor, treewidth is polynomial in maximum degree.
item.dc:creator: Robert Hickingbotham, Freddie Illingworth, Piotr Micek, Bartosz Walczak

item.title: Four colours are needed for closed-neighbourhood conflict-free colouring of all planar graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.22559v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A colouring of the vertices of a graph is conflict-free with respect to closed neighbourhoods if every closed neighbourhood contains a colour that appears on exactly one of its vertices. The colouring need not be proper. Every planar graph has such a colouring with four colours. Fabrici, Lu\v{z}ar, Rindo\v{s}ov\'a and Sot\'ak conjectured that three colours always suffice. We disprove this conjecture. We give a simple gadget construction that turns every planar graph of chromatic number four into a planar graph with no such colouring with three colours. This also shows that it is NP-complete to decide whether three colours suffice for a planar graph. We also give a planar graph on $25$ vertices that needs four colours. Further, we give critical planar graphs on $25$ vertices with $52$ and with $51$ edges, an infinite family of plane triangulations that need four colours, and an infinite family of critical examples.
item.dc:creator: Jelena Sedlar, Riste \v{S}krekovsk

item.title: The Schubert bialgebra
item.description: arXiv:2610.22582v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a Schubert bialgebra $\mathcal{A}=\bigoplus_{n\geq 0}\mathbb{Z}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, in which polynomials in different numbers of variables multiply to zero and the coproduct splits the variables into two consecutive blocks, and study its graded dual $\mathcal{D}$, whose product is concatenation of weak compositions. The Schubert polynomials $\mathfrak{S}_u^n$ form a basis of $\mathcal{A}$; we give an explicit formula for the dual Schubert basis $\Xi_u^n$ of $\mathcal{D}$ via a transition formula to an elementary symmetric basis, and show that the Schubert structure constants $c_{u,v}^w$ are the coefficients of the coproduct of $\mathcal{D}$ in the dual Schubert basis. The product of $\mathcal{D}$ is then lifted to an associative product $\sqcup$ on the free abelian group $\mathcal{BRC}$ of bounded RC graphs, built from a transition map $\mathcal{Z}$ on RC graphs that realizes the Lascoux-Sch\"utzenberger transition formula and generalizes Little's bumping algorithm. Quotienting $\mathcal{BRC}$ by ideals coming from Demazure crystal equivalence, Nadeau-Tewari forest equivalence, and quasi-Yamanouchi equivalence yields manifestly positive Littlewood-Richardson rules for the dual Schubert, dual key, dual forest, and dual slide bases of $\mathcal{D}$. Read on $\mathcal{A}$, these are branching rules: enumerative formulas for splitting a Schubert, key, forest, or slide polynomial across two blocks of variables, and in the Schubert case they compute the Levi branching coefficients of Ressayre-Richmond for $\mathrm{GL}_p\times\mathrm{GL}_q\hookrightarrow\mathrm{GL}_{p+q}$.
item.dc:creator: Matthew J. Samuel

item.title: Complete regular dessins: the nonmetacyclic case
item.description: arXiv:2610.22620v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify regular dessins on $K_{2^e,2^f}$ with nonmetacyclic colour-preserving automorphism group, retaining the two specified vertex rotations. We give nonredundant presentations and exact counts in both the abelian and nonabelian Frattini cases. For orientation- and colour-preserving isomorphisms, the number is $2^{2e-2}+16$ when $e=f\ge4$ and $3\cdot2^{2f-3}+16$ when $e>f\ge4$, with explicit counts for all smaller exponents. The construction uses a parity criterion in the abelian case and a uniquely determined odd quadratic root with two lifts in the nonabelian case. A dessin in the classification is reflexible exactly when its Frattini subgroup is abelian. All symmetric classes are circular. We determine every circular subfamily, including its face orders and genera; the circular count is $2^e+8$ on the diagonal and $2^{f-2}(2^{f-1}+1)+8$ off the diagonal for $e\ge f\ge4$.
item.dc:creator: Kan Hu

item.title: Spectral asymmetry and odd cycles in integral graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.22773v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the triangle $C_3$ is the only integral unicyclic graph with an odd cycle. The main tool is a spectral inequality that does not require integrality: if $G$ is a connected non-bipartite graph and $G-e$ is bipartite for some edge $e$, then the eigenvalues $\lambda_1\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_n$ of $G$ satisfy $\sum_{i}(\lambda_i+\lambda_{n+1-i})^+\le 2$ and $0<\lambda_1+\lambda_n\le 1$. It follows from comparing $A(G)$ with the signed adjacency matrix obtained by reversing the sign of $e$, which is similar to $-A(G)$, through a common rank-one perturbation and Weyl's monotonicity theorem. For integral graphs in this class, an arithmetic lemma then gives $\lambda_n=1-\lambda_1$ and at least $\lambda_1-1\ge1$ triangles, which yields the classification. We also prove that an integral graph of odd girth $g$ has at least $(g-1)!/2$ cycles of length $g$, with equality for the Petersen graph when $g=5$, and we derive consequences for quantum periodicity a
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo O. Braga, Jean Carlo Moraes, Matheus C. Santos

item.title: On the existence of mixed orthogonal arrays of strength two with six factors
item.description: arXiv:2610.22775v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Orthogonal arrays are foundational objects in combinatorial design theory and experimental design theory, with broad applications in computer science, coding theory, and cryptography. In this paper, we investigate the existence for mixed orthogonal arrays of strength two with six factors, and propose several new constructions based on incomplete orthogonal Latin squares, incomplete transversal designs, and $\Sigma$-resolvable transversal designs. As a result, we show that the necessary conditions for the existence of such mixed orthogonal arrays are also sufficient, except for a small number of known exceptions and nine unsettled cases.
item.dc:creator: Xiuling Shan, Guangzhou Chen, Xiangrong Sun

item.title: Counterexamples to the local antimagic leaf conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.22783v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It has been conjectured that $\chi_{\mathrm{la}}(T)\leq\ell(T)+2$ for every tree $T$ of order at least three, where $\chi_{\mathrm{la}}(T)$ is the local antimagic chromatic number and $\ell(T)$ denotes the number of leaves. We disprove this bound and show that no absolute constant can replace $2$ in an inequality of this form. Our approach uses degree-based intervals containing all possible induced vertex weights under bijective edge labelings, together with a separation criterion that forces selected internal vertex weights to be distinct. We first construct caterpillars $T_3$ and $T_4$ satisfying $\chi_{\mathrm{la}}(T_3)=\ell(T_3)+3$ and $\chi_{\mathrm{la}}(T_4)=\ell(T_4)+4$, respectively. We then construct, for every positive integer $r$, infinitely many pairwise nonisomorphic caterpillars with exactly $r$ internal vertices for which every bijective edge labeling is antimagic. Each such caterpillar $T$ satisfies $\chi_{\mathrm{la}}(T)=|V(T)|=\ell(T)+r$. Consequently, $\chi_{\mathrm{la}}(T)-\ell(T)$ is unbounded even within the class of caterpillars, and no absolute constant $C$ can satisfy $\chi_{\mathrm{la}}(T)\leq\ell(T)+C$ for every tree $T$.
item.dc:creator: Andr\'e Ebling Brondani, Francisca Andrea Macedo Fran\c{c}a

item.title: Complete characterization of disconnected one-point unions of cycles with local antimagic chromatic number 2
item.description: arXiv:2610.22808v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A graph $G = (V, E)$ that admits a bijective edge labeling $f:E \to\{1,\ldots ,|E|\}$ is local antimagic if $f$ induces a vertex labeling $f^+$ such that for any pair of adjacent vertices $x$ and $y$, $f^+(x)\not= f^+(y)$, where the induced vertex label $f^+(x)= \sum f(xu)$, with $u$ ranging over all the vertices adjacent to $x$. The minimum number of distinct induced vertex labels over all local antimagic labelings of $G$ is the local antimagic chromatic number of $G$, denoted $\chi_{la}(G)$. In this paper, we completely characterize all the disconnected one-point unions of cycles (having at most 3 components) with local antimagic chromatic number 2. Our approach allows the complete characterization of all such graphs with at least 4 components by a case-by-case analysis and every edge is assigned a unique label, up to isomorphism.
item.dc:creator: Gee-Choon Lau, Wai Chee Shiu

item.title: KKM meets colorful Carath\'eodory
item.description: arXiv:2610.22829v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The colorful Carath\'eodory theorem states that if $V_1,\dots,V_{d+1}\subset\mathbb R^d$ satisfy $0\in\mathrm{conv}\;V_i$ for every $i$, then there exist points $v_i\in V_i$ such that $0\in\mathrm{conv}\;\{v_1,\dots,v_{d+1}\}$. We give a new proof based on triangulations and the classical KKM lemma. We lift the sets $V_i$ to parallel affine copies of $\mathbb R^d$ in $\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^d$ and use a triangulation of the resulting point configuration to construct a KKM cover. Using the same approach, we prove the very colorful Carath\'eodory theorem.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Polyanskii

item.title: The Spectral Theory of Threshold Graphs: A Survey
item.description: arXiv:2610.22838v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Threshold graphs-the $\{P_4, C_4, 2K_2\}$-free graphs, equivalently those built from a single vertex by repeatedly adding isolated or dominating vertices-are among the most thoroughly studied graph classes in spectral graph theory. This survey collects results on the spectrum of threshold graphs across the full range of matrices studied in the literature: the adjacency, Laplacian, and signless Laplacian matrices; the distance, distance Laplacian, and distance signless Laplacian matrices; the eccentricity and Seidel matrices; and the normalized adjacency, Laplacian matrix-together with the associated graph energies, cospectrality questions, extremal spectral radius problems, and several generalizations (weighted, quasi-threshold, hypergraph, and random threshold graphs). We emphasize results from the recent years, including the foundational work of Chv\'atal--Hammer, Merris, Bapat, and Jacobs--Lazzarin--Trevisan--Tura. We also present a study of integral threshold graphs (those with all-integer spectrum) across all seven matrices. We close with a list of open problems and conjectures drawn directly from the surveyed literature and from this new analysis.
item.dc:creator: Pallabi Manna, Santanu Mandal, Fernando C. Tura

item.title: Separable elements and Bruhat orders
item.description: arXiv:2610.22857v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the curious fact that, in any Coxeter group, the intersection of a principal left weak order ideal $[e,x]_L$ with a principal right weak order ideal $[e,y]_R$ has a unique maximal element $\mathrm{lr}(x,y)$ under Bruhat order. We apply this to resolve a conjecture of Hart and Rowley on involutions in weak order ideals. This fact arises from, and is applied to, our study of the theory of separable elements in finite Weyl groups. We use it to prove that for $U=[e,u]_R$ in a Coxeter group $W$, the multiplication map $W/U\times U\rightarrow W$ is surjective, where $W/U$ is the Bj\"{o}rner-Wachs generalized quotient. This resolves and generalizes a conjecture of the authors. For finite Weyl groups, we further prove that this map is bijective if and only if $u$ is separable, thereby classifying the splittings of finite Weyl groups into weak order intervals, and resolving the natural extension of a question of Bj\"orner-Wachs.
item.dc:creator: Christian Gaetz, Yibo Gao

item.title: Overtake and the recursive-line equality for second-order Zarankiewicz numbers
item.description: arXiv:2610.22875v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study two questions about the second-order Zarankiewicz numbers. The first is the recursive-line equality $z_2(m,n)=z_{RL}(m,n)$, known to hold in every computed case and conjectured in general. The second, here called \emph{overtake}, is the strict inequality $z_{2A}(m,n)>z_2(m,n)$ between the second-order augmented number and the second-order number. Both are governed by the number $H_{\mathrm{limited}}(m,n)$ of unoccupied cells in a limited extremal configuration. We prove that the first increase $z_2\to z_2+1$ already costs three unoccupied cells, forcing a unit of one-edge deficit, and the cell identity then bounds the excess $z_{2A}-z_2$ by $\lfloor(H_{\mathrm{limited}}-1)/2\rfloor$. In particular, when the recursive-line hole count is at most two, no overtake occurs. We conjecture the sharp budget $\lfloor H_{\mathrm{limited}}/3\rfloor$ and that $H_{\mathrm{limited}}\ge5$ is the threshold for an overtake. In the computed range $n\le7$, no overtake occurs at any order, the sole exception being the known case $(4,4)$. The recursive-line equality $z_2=z_{RL}$ is verified at every order in the range where both values are determined; the orders at which it remains unsettled are $(12,4)$ and $(14,4)$ at width four, $(11,5)$ at width five, and $(8,7)$ at width seven.
item.dc:creator: Chen Ouyang, Liqun Qi

item.title: Triangle-free Rank--Ramsey graphs from ordered incidence lifts
item.description: arXiv:2610.22902v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a graph $G$ with adjacency matrix $A_G$ and a coefficient field $\mathbb K$, put $\rho_{\mathbb K}(G)=\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb K}(A_G+I)$. We answer the triangle-free Rank--Ramsey existence question of Beniamini, Linial and Shraibman. For every order $n$, we construct a triangle-free graph $H_n$ such that, simultaneously over all coefficient fields, $$ \rho_{\mathbb K}(H_n)=\bigl(4(2/3)^{3/4}+o(1)\bigr)n^{3/4}, $$ with an error uniform in the field. The graphs can be chosen Hamiltonian for all sufficiently large $n$. Our method combines ordered layers of point--line incidence flags with a common low-dimensional endpoint space. We determine the exact real rank, independence number and chromatic number of the affine lifts. For all triangle-free complete incidence lifts, we obtain a sharp two-term lower bound for complete incidence lifts, with sharpness witnessed by projective-plane incidence graphs over suitable coefficient fields. We also establish a third-order estimate and stability near equality. On the same explicit graphs, both the Lov\'asz number and minimum semidefinite rank exceed the prescribed Boolean-matrix rank by polynomial factors. Thus neither parameter has a universal constant-factor upper bound in terms of complement rank. We determine Shannon capacity in the short-layer range.
item.dc:creator: Yong Lu, Qi Wu, Qiannan Zhou

item.title: Sharp Bounds for Common Spanning Forests under Color Refinement
item.description: arXiv:2610.22909v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the common spanning structure of connected finite simple graphs that are indistinguishable by uniformly initialized color refinement. We prove that any two such graphs with common cyclomatic number $r\ge2$ contain isomorphic spanning forests with at most $r-1$ components. This bound depends only on $r$ and is sharp for every $r\ge2$. We also determine the maximum, over all such graph pairs without restricting their order, of the minimum edge symmetric difference under vertex bijections: it is exactly $4(r-1)$.
item.dc:creator: Jianshen Zhu

item.title: Enumeration of small vertex-transitive directed strongly regular graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.22938v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We find the 728 vertex-transitive directed strongly regular graphs with parameters $(v,k,t,\lambda,\mu)$ where $1 \le v \le 39$ and $k < v/2$ and $0 < t < k$. A table with parameters and automorphism groups and some additional data is given.
item.dc:creator: A. E. Brouwer, \v{S}. Gy\"urki

item.title: An Erd\H{o}s-P\'osa theorem for induced packings of even cycles
item.description: arXiv:2610.22967v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that for every graph $G$ and every positive integer $k$, $G$ contains either $k$ vertex-disjoint even cycles with no edges between distinct cycles, or a set of $O(k^2\log k)$ vertices whose closed neighborhood meets every even cycle of $G$. Moreover, we give a polynomial-time algorithm that outputs one of the two outcomes. As an application, we show that every $K_{1,t}$-free graph containing no induced packing of $k$ even cycles has tree-independence number $O(tk^2\log k)$, with a corresponding decomposition computable in polynomial time.
item.dc:creator: Jungho Ahn, Lars Jaffke, O-joung Kwon, Paloma T. de Lima, Hyemi Park

item.title: Hypergraphs of Low Degree Without Independent Transversals
item.description: arXiv:2610.22993v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every fixed $k\ge 3$ and every integer $b\ge 2$, we construct a finite vertex-partitioned $k$-uniform hypergraph with blocks of size $b$ and no independent transversal. We show that the maximum number of edges meeting a block is $\left(\frac{(k-1)^{k-1}}{k^k}+O_k(b^{-1})\right)b^k,$ while the maximum vertex degree is $\left(\frac{(k-2)^{k-2}}{(k-1)^{k-1}}+O_k(b^{-1})\right)b^{k-1}$. This shows that the known bound on the number of edges meeting a block is asymptotically sharp even when the leading constant in the maximum vertex degree tends to zero, which answers a problem of Groenland, Kaiser, Treffers, and Wales. By blowing up the same construction, we further obtain for arbitrarily large $n$, there exists a $k$-uniform hypergraph with $n$ blocks, each of size at least $n$, and $\Delta(G)<\left(1-\frac1k\right)^{k-1}n^{k-1}$, but with no independent transversal. This gives a negative answer to a problem of Haxell and Wdowinski.
item.dc:creator: Xinzhe Song, Xia Wang

item.title: A cubulation of the associahedron using a torus-equivariant degeneration of the brick variety
item.description: arXiv:2610.23004v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We describe a mixed subdivision of the $(n-1)$-dimensional Loday associahedron into $(n-1)!$ maximal cells which are combinatorial cubes, and we show that the face poset of this subdivision is isomorphic to the face poset of the subdivision of the $1\times 2\times \dotsb \times (n-1)$ box into unit cubes. More generally, we describe mixed subdivisions of generalized associahedra into pieces which are Minkowski sums of Bruhat interval polytopes. Our subdivisions arise from a torus-equivariant embedded (in a product of flag varieties) degeneration of brick varieties into reduced unions of products of Richardson varieties. The subdivision of Loday's associahedron allows us to `embed' the 1-skeleton of the permutahedron in the boundary of the associahedron.
item.dc:creator: Raj Gandhi, Gabe Udell

item.title: Counterexamples to Two Conjectures on Tangles in Matroid Minors
item.description: arXiv:2610.23059v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give counterexamples to two conjectures of Brettell, Jowett, Oxley, Semple, and Whittle concerning tangles in matroid minors. We construct a matroid $P_0$ with a tangle $\mathcal T$ of order seven. For each $i\in\{4,5,6,7\}$, let $\mathcal T_i$ denote its order-$i$ truncation. No proper minor $N$ of $P_0$ admits, for every such $i$, a tangle of order $i$ whose breadth equals that of $\mathcal T_i$, and $P_0$ is not weakly $4$-connected. We also construct a matroid $P_1$ with a tangle of order four and breadth six, but no internally $4$-connected minor of $P_1$ admits a tangle of order four.
item.dc:creator: Zhen Chen, Zhuo Li

item.title: A Generating Polynomial for Convex Subsets of Posets
item.description: arXiv:2610.23399v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For any finite poset we define a generating polynomial counting upsets, downsets, and their intersection. We investigate the behaviour of this polynomial with respect to poset operations and show that it distinguishes certain posets constructed with the operations of ordinal sum and disjoint union, including Series-Parallel posets as a special case. Lastly, we comment on connections to the causal set approach to quantum gravity.
item.dc:creator: Ian George, Rowan Yeats

item.title: Odd Cycle Decompositions
item.description: arXiv:2610.23471v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the asymptotic minimum-degree threshold for decompositions into cycles of every fixed odd length. We prove that, for each odd integer $\ell\ge3$, every $\eps>0$ and sufficiently large $n$, every $n$-vertex $C_\ell$-divisible graph $G$ with minimum degree $\delta(G)\ge (\ell/(2\ell-2)+\eps)n$ has a $C_\ell$-decomposition, where $C_{\ell}$ denotes the cycle of length $\ell$. The constant is best possible. This settles the remaining cases $\ell=5,7,\ldots,71$ and completes the determination of the thresholds for all odd cycles. The proof combines the condensation approach of Bryant et al. with a sharp weighted-triangle fractional decomposition theorem. Its key step is a rescaling of the dual edge weights that allows us to apply a quantitative discharging estimate from the breakthrough of Delcourt and Postle on Nash--Williams' triangle decomposition conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Jianfeng Hou, Caiyun Hu, Hezhi Wang

item.title: Small and large quasi-kernels: a weighted transfer theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.23487v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A quasi-kernel of a digraph $D$ is an independent set from which every vertex is reachable by a directed path of length at most two. The Small Quasi-kernel Conjecture asserts that every source-free digraph on $n$ vertices has a quasi-kernel of size at most $n/2$, whereas the Large Quasi-kernel Conjecture asks for a quasi-kernel whose closed out-neighbourhood has size at least $n/2$. Spiro proved that the former implies the latter. In this paper, we establish a weighted transfer theorem: if every nonnegative integer weighting of a source-free digraph $D$ admits a quasi-kernel whose closed out-neighbourhood contains at least a $\theta$-fraction of the total weight, then $D$ has a quasi-kernel of size at most $\lfloor(1-\theta)\alpha(D)+\theta\mu\rfloor$ for $0<\theta\le1/2$, where $\mu$ is the maximum matching size between a maximum independent set and its complement. Using the independent blow-up construction of Spiro, we deduce that the universal small and large quasi-kernel assertions are equivalent for every such $\theta$, with no loss in the parameter. In particular, the two conjectures are equivalent. As an application, we prove the half-order bound for source-free break digraphs.
item.dc:creator: Jiangdong Ai, Gregory Gutin, Xiangzhou Liu, Xianhao Meng

item.title: Visibility Sets, Empty Pentagons, and Sufficient Conditions for Hexagons
item.description: arXiv:2610.23553v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a set $S$ of $n$ points in general position in the plane, we define the $C$-set $C(p,q)$ of an oriented edge $(p,q)$ as the set of extreme points of the visibility set $V(p,q)$ facing $(p,q)$. Since every point of $V(p,q)$ that is not in $C(p,q)$ gives rise to an empty convex pentagon having $(p,q)$ as a boundary edge, it is natural to study the properties of $C$-sets in order to bound the number of empty convex pentagons of $S$. We prove tight bounds on the intersection size and union complexity of $C$-sets sharing an endpoint. We also consider the problem of bounding the number of empty pentagons and hexagons in terms of the number of interior and boundary points of $S$. While the hexagon bound is weak, it offers a potential step toward a superlinear lower bound. On the other hand, the two-parameter bound for pentagons, combined with the structural results on $C$-sets, yields a simple proof of an $\Omega(n^{3/2})$ bound for the number of pentagons. While this is a significant improvement over previously published bounds, a recent preprint \cite{Astudillo2026} attains a better bound using completely different methods. Thus, the primary contribution of this paper lies in the structural results about $C$-sets and the two-parameter bounds for empty pentagons and hexagons.
item.dc:creator: Carlos M. Nicolas

item.title: Line spreads of W(2n-1, q), q even
item.description: arXiv:2610.23664v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let q be an even prime power and n \ge 2. We construct line spreads of the symplectic polar space W(2n-1,q) by replacing pairwise disjoint reguli in a Desarguesian line spread. The construction is based on partitions of the points of PG(n-1,q^2) into points of a nondegenerate Hermitian variety and Baer sublines meeting that variety in exactly one point. In the plane case, the partition is invariant under a cyclic group of order q^2-q+ 1.
item.dc:creator: Daniele Bartoli, Antonio Cossidente, Giuseppe Marino, Francesco Pavese

item.title: The maximum number of Hamiltonian cycles in tournaments
item.description: arXiv:2610.23755v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $C(n)$ denote the maximum number of directed Hamiltonian cycles in a tournament on $n$ vertices. We prove that, as $n\to\infty$, $$ C(n) = \left(\frac{\cosh 1}{\cos 1}\pm o(1)\right)\frac{(n-1)!}{2^n}. $$ The bound is asymptotically attained by the regular tournament with vertices $\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z$ where $(i,j)$ is a directed edge if $j - i \pmod n< n/2$. This answers a question of Alon and proves a conjecture of Wormald. Among the other implications of these results is asymptotically determining the maximum number of Hamiltonian paths in a tournament on $n$ vertices. We provide our own exposition of these proofs, which were originally found by GPT-5.6.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Divoux, Shouda Wang

item.title: Revisiting separators in string graphs, region intersection graphs, and induced-minor-free graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.23792v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: String graphs are intersection graphs of continuous curves in the plane. In 2010, Fox and Pach proved that string graphs with $m$ edges admit balanced vertex separators of size $\mathcal{O}(m^{3/4}\sqrt{\log m})$ and conjectured that this bound can be improved to $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{m})$, which would be optimal. After partial progress, Lee claimed in 2017 to prove this conjecture, and more generally to prove analogous separator theorems for region intersection graphs over minor-closed graph families. A key intermediate step in Lee's approach was a padded decomposition scheme for region intersection graphs. In 2024, Korhonen and Lokshtanov extended Lee's approach to the broader setting of graph classes excluding a fixed graph as an induced minor. These results have since found applications in a wide range of works. Later in 2024, a flaw was discovered in the construction of Lee's padded decomposition scheme, invalidating Lee's as well as Korhonen and Lokshtanov's separator results, and many works relying on them. In this work, we prove that string graphs with $m$ edges admit balanced separators of size $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{m})$, and more generally obtain analogous $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{m})$ bounds for region intersection graphs over fixed minor-closed graph families and for graphs excluding a fixed graph as an induced minor, thereby repairing the vast majority of the affected works. Furthermore, our balanced separators can be found in polynomial time. Our proof uses a different approach from Lee's and does not rely on padded decompositions. Since padded decompositions have also found applications independent of the separator theorems, particularly for string graphs, we also prove a padded decomposition result for region intersection graphs that is optimal for string graphs. We have formalized both the balanced separator and the padded decomposition results in Lean 4 with mathlib.
item.dc:creator: James Davies, Pawe{\l} Rz\k{a}\.zewski, Jack Spalding-Jamieson, Bartosz Walczak

item.title: Eventual Exactness and Rigidity for Abelian Covers of Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.22388v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a group $G$, let $a(G)$ denote the minimum number of abelian subgroups covering $G$, and let $\omega(G)$ be the maximum size of a pairwise noncommuting set. We prove the exact formula $\sup_{\omega(G)\leq n}a(G)=2^{\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor}+1$ for every $n\geq 63$. Equality holds precisely for groups with derived subgroup of order two and binary symplectic central quotient of dimension $2\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor$. The proof combines centralizer descent with a structural separation of nonscalar alternating commutator maps.
item.dc:creator: Guillaume Lecomte

item.title: Quantum Periods from TBA and Continued Fractions
item.description: arXiv:2610.22571v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider quantum A-periods of local ${\mathbb P}^1 \times {\mathbb P}^1$, or equivalently the generating function of constant terms for powers of the Laurent polynomial $x + x^{-1} + y + y^{-1}$ where $x$ and $y$ are $q$-commuting variables. We derive a number of new representations for these rich combinatorial and algebraic objects. First, we find that the well-known TBA equation encodes not only the A-period itself but also higher diagonal modes of the corresponding noncommutative Laurent polynomials. Second, we obtain new formulas for the period in terms of continued fractions and related orthogonal polynomials, as well as a nontrivial explicit recursion allowing its efficient computation. Finally, we compute quantum corrections to the classical Picard-Fuchs equation, and observe that holonomicity of the classical period does not generalise to $q$-holonomicity of its quantum counterpart. Applications to random walks on the Cayley graph of the Heisenberg group, and related new approaches to more efficient generative AI systems, are outlined.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Chervov, Ilia Gaiur, Sergey Galkin, Fedor Levkovich-Maslyuk, Volodya Rubtsov, Shamil Shakirov

item.title: Axis-parallel square packing with an exact formula for optimal packing of seven squares
item.description: arXiv:2610.22622v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: How large a square is needed to hold axis-parallel squares of prescribed side lengths? We give exact formulas for the optimal side through seven squares, with explicit constructions and geometric lower-bound proofs. For every $n\ge6$, the optimum for $n$ squares is a sum of at most $n-3$ of the prescribed side lengths. This bound is sharp on an open set of side lengths and yields the optimal Euclidean Lipschitz constant $\sqrt{n-3}$ of the optimum as a function of the $n$ side lengths.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Badger

item.title: Singular vectors of sparse random rectangular matrices: Transition between delocalized and semilocalized phases
item.description: arXiv:2610.22658v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Consider the bipartite Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi graph $\mathbb{G}(n,m,d/\sqrt{mn})$ at the critical sparsity $d = b\log(N)$ for some $b > 0$ with $N = n + m$, and constant aspect ratio $\gamma = n/m \geq 1$. We show that the spectrum of its centered and rescaled bi-adjacency matrix, whose limiting law is the Mar\v{c}enko--Pastur (MP) distribution, is split into two phases: in the bulk, singular vectors are completely delocalized, while near the edges, singular vectors are semilocalized, with their mass concentrating on small disjoint balls, centered at vertices with extreme degrees. As $b$ decreases, we identify sharp thresholds for the emergence of outlier singular values. For explicit $b_{\rm R}^{\star}$ and $b_{\rm L}^{\star}$ as functions of $\gamma$, we prove that when $b > b_{\rm R}^{\star}$, there is no outlier outside the bulk; when $b_{\rm L}^{\star}< b < b_{\rm R}^{\star}$, only right outliers emerge; and when $b < b_{\rm L}^{\star}$, outliers are present on both sides, all with high probability. This removes an extra technical condition from our previous work arxiv:2508.01456, providing a complete characterization of the parameter space. In sparser regimes, in terms of left outliers, we provide some nontrivial generating mechanisms, demonstrating that local graph structure plays a key role in understanding extreme singular values. Our proofs rely on two technical inputs: (1) an entrywise local law in the MP bulk, where the deterministic equivalent of the resolvent depends on both variance profiles and normalized vertex degrees, different from the Gaussian setting; (2) spectral radius upper bounds for nonbacktracking matrices constructed from regularized random graphs, recently developed in arXiv: 2609.26615. Our results reveal fruitful phenomena for sparse random rectangular matrices at criticality, which are beyond the universality class of their Gaussian counterparts.
item.dc:creator: Ioana Dumitriu, Hai-Xiao Wang

item.title: Rational decomposition of polyhedra and a conjecture of Brlek and Reutenauer
item.description: arXiv:2610.22663v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove in the affirmative a conjecture of Brlek and Reutenauer (2003), which relates unambiguous rational sets to a well known result due to Khovanskii and Pukhlikov (1992) and independently to Lawrence (1990) on the valuations of the algebra spanned by the indicator functions of polyhedra.
item.dc:creator: Flavio D'Alessandro, Paolo Papi

item.title: String functions and cyclotomic Hecke algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.22669v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper we study the Kleshchev multipartitions that label simple modules of certain cyclotomic Hecke algebras with parameters $1$ and $-1$. The $2$-residue statistic divides these multipartitions into blocks. We deduce a bivariate generating function for the blocks using representation theory. We also relate the generating functions of multipartitions in a fixed block to string functions associated by Kac and Peterson to irreducible highest weight modules of a type $A_1^{(1)}$ affine Lie algebra. By considering matrices formed by these generating functions, we reprove some results of Kac--Peterson on string functions using the Macdonald identities of Rosengren--Schlosser. As an application, we obtain new infinite product formulas for these generating functions.
item.dc:creator: Dennis Stanton, Ting Xue, Ae Ja Yee

item.title: Hypercube Richardson varieties from magic words
item.description: arXiv:2610.22730v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Inspired by the recent preprint of Ellenberg, Libedinsky, Plaza, Simental, and Williamson, we study the geometry of Richardson varieties whose associated Bruhat intervals are boolean posets. We define magic words for a Bruhat interval and prove that for intervals with magic words the associated Richardson variety is a tower of $\mathbb{P}^1$-s. We also prove that the Bruhat intervals consisting of the dyadically well-distributed permutations all have magic words. This gives a new proof that they form a boolean poset.
item.dc:creator: Bal\'azs Elek

item.title: Signed dual graphs and face spectral gaps of Cayley 2-complexes
item.description: arXiv:2610.22916v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a weighted signed dual multigraph for the Cayley $2$-complex of a finite presentation and represent its $\ell^2$ face Laplacian as a signed graph Laplacian with a diagonal potential. We prove that the face spectral gap above the kernel vanishes for the Baumslag--Solitar groups $\operatorname{BS}(1,m)$, $m\ge2$, using explicit finitely supported face chains. Our main vanishing theorem gives the same conclusion for every finitely presented amenable group with ordinary first Betti number at least two.
item.dc:creator: Bobo Hua, Yong Lin, Tao Wang, Haohang Zhang

item.title: Sharp asymptotics for the Lov\'asz number of random circulant graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.22971v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the LOV\'ASZ number of dense random circulant graphs generated by independent Bernoulli bits indexed by cyclic distances. Although only $O(n)$ independent random inputs determine $O(n^2)$ globally dependent edge indicators, we prove sharp expectation asymptotics along all odd orders, including composite orders, with leading constant one. This resolves a conjecture posed for random circulant graphs in 2025. The proof combines an exact Fourier reduction and complementary duality with a positive interior smoothing that reveals a nonlinear random fixed-point equation. To analyze this equation under the strong dependence of the distance-bit model, we construct canonical tree fields, establish growing-degree Gaussian approximations through polynomial comparison and Wick/Hermite expansions, and transfer the resulting approximation back to the original sign model. A deterministic residual estimate together with an explicit exceptional-event integration yields the sharp expectation asymptotics.
item.dc:creator: Xin Chen, Hongwei Hu, Yanqing Hu, Wei Wang, Luzhen Yang

item.title: Perron-Wright asymptotics and critical component processes for regular inhomogeneous random graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.23003v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We extend Wright's enumeration of connected labelled graphs with fixed surplus to irreducible critical finite type kernels and regular compact type kernels. Let $C_t(k,r)$ denote the total weight of connected labelled graphs with $k$ vertices and surplus $r$. Let $u>0$ satisfy $Ku=u$ and $\int u\,d\mu=1$, and put $\alpha=\int u^2\,d\mu$ and $\beta=\int u^3\,d\mu$. We prove that the rooted-tree radius $\rho$ is positive and real analytic near $1$, with $\rho(1)=1$ and $\log\rho(t)=\frac{\alpha^2}{2\beta}(t-1)^2+O(|t-1|^3)$, and that, for fixed $r\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$ and $0\le L < \infty$, $C_t(k,r)=w_r\beta^{(r-1)/2}e^{-k}\rho(t)^{-k}k^{k+3r/2-2}\{1+O_{r,L}(k^{-1/2})\}$, uniformly for $|t-1|\le Lk^{-1/2}$, where $w_r$ is the classical Wright constant. At $t_n=1+\lambda n^{-1/3}$, these asymptotics yield local size and surplus point-process limits for deterministic finite type models and annealed compact type Bollobas-Janson-Riordan models satisfying projective quadratic regularity. After rescaling component sizes by $\beta^{1/3}n^{-2/3}$, the limit is the Aldous process at parameter $\alpha\beta^{-2/3}\lambda$, and the corresponding type profiles concentrate at the Perron law $p(dx)=u(x)\mu(dx)$. For every regular countable critical kernel, we construct graph sequences with growing finite supports and the same local limits, and identify the additive shift of the critical window caused by spectral perturbations of order $n^{-1/3}$.
item.dc:creator: Wentao Hu, Wen Sun

item.title: Comparing word probabilities in finite groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.23100v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We use results from extremal graph theory and analysis to compare word probabilities in finite groups. In particular, we show that the probability of satisfying the 2-Engel word admits a positive lower bound in terms of the probability that an element has order dividing 3. More generally, using a group removal lemma, we obtain analogous bounds for $x^m$-good words.
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo Putignano, Matteo Vannacci

item.title: Minimal asymptotic \(g\)-adic bases from arbitrary partitions
item.description: arXiv:2610.23152v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $g>h\ge2$ be integers. For a nonempty set $W\subseteq\N$, let $\mathcal F^*(W)$ denote the set of its finite nonempty subsets. Let $$A_g(W)=\left\{\sum_{f\in F}a_fg^f: 1\leq a_f \leq g-1,F \in \mathcal F^*(W)\right\},$$ and let $\N=W_1\sqcup\cdots\sqcup W_h$ be a partition into infinite sets. We prove that $A=\bigcup_{i=1}^h A_g(W_i)$ is a minimal asymptotic basis of order $h$ for every such partition.
item.dc:creator: Min Tang

item.title: Regularity, depth and Serre depth of symbolic powers of complementary edge ideals
item.description: arXiv:2610.23224v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph and let $I_c(G)$ denote its complementary edge ideal. In this paper, we study the Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity, the depth and Serre depth for $(S_{2})$ of the symbolic powers of $I_c(G)$. We derive explicit formulas for $\operatorname{reg} I_c(G)^{(k)}$ and $\operatorname{reg} I_c(G)^{(k)}/I_c(G)^k$ for every $k\geq1$, in terms of the number and the sizes of the connected components of $G$. As applications, we determine their asymptotic behavior, and completely characterize the symbolic powers of complementary edge ideals having linear resolutions. We then investigate the symbolic depth function $k\mapsto\operatorname{depth} S/I_c(G)^{(k)}$. We determine explicitly its values for $k=2,3,4$, and establish bounds for the asymptotic depth. More generally, for an arbitrary squarefree monomial ideal $I$, we compare the local cohomology modules of $S/I^{(k)}$ for different symbolic powers, and derive corresponding inequalities for the depth and the Serre depth. Applying this to complementary edge ideals, we obtain $\operatorname{depth} S/I_{c}(G)^{(t)}\geq\operatorname{depth} S/I_{c}(G)^{(k)}$ for $k\geq 2t-1$, despite the fact that the symbolic depth function need not be non-increasing. Finally, we characterize complementary edge ideals satisfying Serre's condition $(S_r)$, and determine the Serre depth for $(S_{2})$ of all symbolic powers of complementary edge ideals. In particular, we obtain combinatorial characterizations of Serre's condition $(S_{2})$ and of the Cohen-Macaulayness of $S/I_{c}(G)^{(k)}$ for every $k\geq 1$.
item.dc:creator: Antonino Ficarra, Somayeh Moradi, Yuji Muta

item.title: A Generalized Half-Singleton Bound for List Decoding of Insertion/Deletion Errors
item.description: arXiv:2610.23270v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We derive an upper bound on the rate of a linear code capable of list decoding from insertion and deletion errors. Subsequently, we show that a linear code can list decode from at most $n - \frac{L}{L+1}k + 1$ insdel errors with fixed list size $L$, and that this bound is strict when the code does not contain the all-ones vector. We also provide a simple construction of codes achieving the optimal rate for any given list size capable of correcting a single insdel error. All the results hold for linear codes over finite fields of size $q \geq 3$.
item.dc:creator: Neehar Verma, Camilla Hollanti, Razane Tajeddine

item.title: The Strong Total Cover Problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.23312v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Strong Total Cover Problem (STCP) is a novel covering problem defined on a graph $G = (V, E)$, where the objective is to find a minimum-cardinality subset $T \subseteq V \cup E$ such that every element of $V \cup E$ is covered. In this setting, a vertex covers itself and all its incident edges, while an edge covers itself together with its two endpoints. The STCP resembles classical covering problems such as Vertex Cover and Edge Cover problems, and naturally arises as the dual of the total matching problem. In this paper, we investigate the STCP from algorithmic, complexity, and polyhedral perspectives. We first establish close connections between STCP, the Dominating Set Problem, and the Maximum Induced Matching Problem. These relationships provide structural insights, imply the NP-hardness of STCP, and identify graph classes for which the problem is polynomial-time solvable. We then investigate the weighted version of STCP, showing that it remains NP-hard even on complete graphs with binary weights. On the other hand, we present a 2-approximation algorithm, and a polynomial-time algorithm for complete bipartite graphs. On the polyhedral side, we introduce the Strong Total Cover Polytope and derive several families of valid inequalities, some of which are shown to define facets. Finally, we provide a complete linear description of the associated polytope for triangular cactus graphs, revealing an interesting contrast with the considerably more intricate facial structure of the dominating set polytope on cactus graphs.
item.dc:creator: Manuel Aprile, Luca Ferrarini

item.title: Finiteness of planar central configurations of six bodies for all positive masses: Part I, exceptional-mass first limits
item.description: arXiv:2610.23329v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We separate the generic positive-mass finiteness problem for planar six-body central configurations from finiteness on exceptional mass loci. The Chang--Chen diagram enumeration has 117 graphs. The arguments below confine 40 first-limit diagram obligations to proper necessary mass loci. In particular, a direct function-field argument establishes the No.~66 mass condition for both zero and nonzero drift. We establish the algebraic reduction from an infinite positive family to a germ with an unbounded seven-product, and use the stated diagram rules and computational certificates to confine its mass vector to the union of these loci. Finiteness on the exceptional positive mass loci, the proposed subject of Part II, will be discussed in another paper.
item.dc:creator: Zhe Chen, Zhicheng Tong

item.title: Entropy estimates and volume rigidity for graphs with positive Bakry-\'Emery curvature
item.description: arXiv:2610.23417v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish a volume bound for weighted graphs with positive Bakry--\'Emery curvature through entropy estimates for the heat flow and characterize the equality case. As a consequence, if a connected unweighted graph $G=(V,E)$ satisfies the Bakry--\'Emery curvature--dimension condition $CD(2,\infty)$ with respect to the unnormalized Laplacian, then $$ |V|\le 2^d, $$ where $d$ denotes the maximum degree. Equality holds if and only if $G$ is a hypercube. We also establish an analogous volume rigidity result for the normalized Laplacian.
item.dc:creator: Yanlong Ding, Shiping Liu, Chiyu Zhou

item.title: Subvariety intervals and limit varieties of zero extensions of mirror-word semirings
item.description: arXiv:2610.23478v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For the mirror word $\mathbf{m}_n=a_1\cdots a_na_n\cdots a_1$, let $\mathcal{V}_n=\mathrm{V}(S(\mathbf{m}_n))$ and $\mathcal{W}_n=\mathrm{V}(S(\mathbf{m}_n)^0)$. We show that $[\mathcal{W}_n,\mathcal{W}_{n+1}]$ ($n\geq 1$) and $[\mathcal{V}_n,\mathcal{W}_n]$ ($n\geq 2$) have cardinality $2^{\aleph_0}$. Every variety in $[\mathcal{W}_2,\mathcal{W}_\infty]$ has infinite axiomatic rank. The unique limit subvariety of $\mathcal{W}_1$ is $\mathrm{V}(SR_6)$. For $n\geq 2$, we construct a distinct directed-path limit variety contained in $\mathcal{W}_n$ but not in $\mathcal{V}_n$.
item.dc:creator: Ruijing Wang, Mengya Yue

item.title: Four New Single-Error-Correcting Binary Codes
item.description: arXiv:2610.23626v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a $(16, 3072, 3)$-code, a $(17,6144,3)$-code, an $(18,12288,3)$-code and a $(19,24576,3)$-code. Consequently, we get four new lower bounds: $A(16,3) \geq 3072$, $A(17,3) \geq 6144$, $A(18,3) \geq 12288$ and $A(19,3) \geq~24576$. Each of the codes consists of a union of cosets of a linear code. The constructions are the result of a computer search executing a tabu search algorithm.
item.dc:creator: Moshe Milshtein

item.title: On the Length of Maximum Sum-Rank Distance Codes
item.description: arXiv:2610.23633v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The classical theory of arcs in finite projective spaces provides a powerful geometric framework for studying maximum distance separable (MDS) codes and their possible lengths. In this paper, we investigate how this perspective extends to maximum sum-rank distance (MSRD) codes, whose geometric description involves systems of linear sets rather than individual projective points. Our main goal is to understand how the block structure of an MSRD code constrains its length. In dimension three, we determine the possible intersection patterns of lines with the associated linear sets and obtain explicit formulas for their characters and the weight distribution of the corresponding codes. These results lead to new length bounds and show that the block structure comes at a cost: the presence of a block of rank at least two reduces the maximum possible total length by at least $q-1$, and sufficiently long MSRD codes must be classical, that is, MDS codes over $\mathbb F_{q^m}$. We also prove that three-dimensional one-weight MSRD codes do not exist. In arbitrary dimension, we interpret shortening geometrically as projection and establish a general projection bound that extends classical counting arguments for arcs. This yields restrictions depending explicitly on the block profile and, for full-length blocks, identifies parameter ranges in which linearized Reed--Solomon codes attain the maximum possible number of blocks. Finally, we construct an exceptional three-dimensional MSRD code over $\mathbb F_9$ with three blocks of length two and propose a sum-rank analogue of the MDS conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Valentina Astore, Ferdinando Zullo

item.title: The semiring of spectral duality skeletons: cancellation, characters and factorization
item.description: arXiv:2610.23684v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Weighted dual skeletons are the combinatorial core of spectral duality structures. Their isomorphism classes, under Cartesian product and disjoint union, form a semiring graded by the degree. We identify it completely: a class is determined by its degree, a symmetric element of the group semiring N_0[R] and its number of fixed points. Equivalently, skeletons of a given degree are finite C_2-sets over the C_2-monoid (R,+), these data are their marks, and the semiring is an infinite-monoid analogue of a crossed Burnside semiring. The multiplicative monoid is not cancellative, the only obstruction being that multiplication by a skeleton without fixed points forgets the fixed points; accordingly, the Grothendieck ring has explicit zero divisors. A continuous family of semiring characters, with the degree and the number of fixed points, is a complete invariant, and for commensurable ratios the multiplicative Grothendieck group is described by P\'olya's theorem. The main subject is factorization. The reduced monoid is atomic with bounded lengths, but factorization is not unique, the elasticity is infinite, and even the divisor-closed submonoid with one fixed point is not half-factorial. Without fixed points, every reducible skeleton splits off a single orbit, which gives a criterion by centers, exactly when the number of orbits is 8, 16, a prime or twice a prime. Irreducibility is generic in almost every type. Progression skeletons factor according to mixed-radix number systems, with all factorizations of equal length. Finally, orbit counting gives the dimension of the separatrix and the response rank of products.
item.dc:creator: Juan Antonio Vega Coso

item.title: Near optimal gap in the Lonely Runner Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.23790v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a set $V$ of $n$ distinct positive integers, let $\mathrm{ML}(V)=\max_{t\in\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}}\min_{v\in V}\|vt\|$, where $\|x\|$ is the distance from $x$ to the nearest integer. We prove that there is an absolute constant $c>0$ such that for every $n\ge2$ and every $V$, \[ \mathrm{ML}(V)>\frac{1+c}{2n}. \] The proof combines a refinement of the large GCD argument of Green and Walker with a new physical spillover inequality for interval multiplicities.
item.dc:creator: Xiyu Hu, Yifan Jing

item.title: Symplectic Lie groups and nilmanifolds associated with acyclic quivers
item.description: arXiv:2610.23794v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give combinatorial criteria for the existence of left-invariant symplectic forms on the positive and full path Lie groups of finite acyclic quivers. For the nilpotent positive path Lie groups, the criterion also determines whether their compact quotients admit symplectic forms and forces the nilpotency step to be at most three. For the completely solvable full path Lie groups, we give a direct combinatorial criterion and an equivalent recursive criterion. In the symplectic case, the recursive procedure is realized by successive Hamiltonian reductions ending at an abelian symplectic Lie group. We characterize the existence of Lagrangian normal subgroups for a given form in both families, with applications to Lagrangian torus fibrations of compact nilmanifolds. We also describe the cohomology rings of the compact symplectic nilmanifolds and determine all Lefschetz ranks.
item.dc:creator: Yihao Zheng

item.title: Observations on the hex clusters of the Spectre tilings
item.description: arXiv:2407.05359v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Decorating the Spectre tile with hexagons reveals triangular hexagonal clusters whose structure we study. In the process we reprove that the Spectre tilings exist and are uniquely hierarchical. The proof is not computer-assisted.
item.dc:creator: Arnaud Ch\'eritat

item.title: Bounds on the Complete Forcing Numbers of Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2409.17306v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A complete forcing set of a graph is a subset $S$ of its edges with the following property. For any perfect matching $M$, $M$ is the unique perfect matching containing the intersection of $M$ and $S$. The size of a smallest complete forcing set of a graph is called its complete forcing number. In this paper, we propose a polynomial-time algorithm that takes a graph and an ordering of its vertices as input, and outputs a complete forcing set. We analyze the size of the output for a carefully chosen ordering to derive an upper bound on the complete forcing numbers of graphs in terms of other graph-theoretical parameters, such as the degeneracy and the spectral radius of the underlying graph. We compare our results with previous findings in the field. For the class of edge-transitive graphs, we provide an explicit lower bound on the complete forcing number. This result is applied in particular to hypercube graphs and Cartesian powers of even cycles.
item.dc:creator: Javad B. Ebrahimi, Aref Namayandeh, Elahe Tohidi

item.title: $(2k+1)$-Neighborhood Balanced Coloring
item.description: arXiv:2505.07758v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $G=(V,E)$ be a simple graph and $(2k+1)$ be a prime integer. Let each vertex of $G$ be colored using one of the $(2k+1)$ colors, say $R_1,R_2,...,R_{2k+1}$. If every vertex has an equal number of neighbors of each color, then the coloring is a $(2k+1)$-neighborhood balanced coloring. We establish a number of results for common families of graphs and present some families of graphs that have this property.
item.dc:creator: Maurice Genevieva Almeida

item.title: The largest sets of non-opposite chambers in spherical buildings of type $B$
item.description: arXiv:2505.14322v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The investigation into large families of non-opposite flags in finite spherical buildings has been a recent addition to a long line of research in extremal combinatorics, extending classical results in vector and polar spaces. This line of research falls under the umbrella of Erd\H{o}s-Ko-Rado (EKR) problems, but poses some extra difficulty on the algebraic level compared to aforementioned classical results. From the building theory point of view, it can be seen as a variation of the center conjecture for spherical buildings due to Tits, where we replace the convexity assumption by a maximality condition. In previous work, general upper bounds on the size of families of non-opposite flags were obtained by applying eigenvalue and representation-theoretic techniques to the Iwahori-Hecke algebras of non-exceptional buildings. More recently, the classification of families reaching this upper bound in type $A_n$, for $n$ odd, was accomplished by Heering, Lansdown, and Metsch. For buildings of type $B$, the corresponding Iwahori-Hecke algebra is more complicated and depends non-trivially on the type and rank of the underlying polar space. Nevertheless, we are able to find a uniform method based on antidesigns and obtain classification results for chambers (i.e.\ maximal flags) in most cases.
item.dc:creator: Jan De Beule, Philipp Heering, Sam Mattheus, Klaus Metsch

item.title: Existence of 3 anti-cocircular truncated M\"obius planes and constructions of strength-4 covering arrays
item.description: arXiv:2510.13122v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Two projective (affine) planes with the same point sets are orthogoval if the common intersection of any two lines, one from each, has size at most two. The existence of a pair of orthogoval projective planes has been proven and published independently many times. A strength-$t$ covering array, denoted by CA$(N; t, k, v)$, is an $N \times k$ array over a $v$-set such that in any $t$-set of columns, each $t$-tuple occurs at least once in a row. A pair of orthogoval projective planes can be used to construct a strength-$3$ covering array CA$(2q^3-1; 3, q^2 + q + 1, q)$. Our work extends this result to construct arrays of strength $4$. A $k$-cap in a projective geometry is a set of $k$ points no three of which are collinear. In $PG(3,q)$, an ovoid is a maximum-sized $k$-cap with $k =q^2+1$. Its plane sections (circles) are the blocks of a $3-(q^2 + 1, q + 1, 1)$ design, called a M\"obius plane of order $q$. For $q$ an odd prime power, we prove the existence of three truncated M\"obius planes, such that for any choice of these circles, one from each plane, their intersection size is at most three. From this, we construct a strength-$4$ covering array CA$(3q^4-2; 4, \frac{q^2+1}{2}, q)$. For $q \geq 11$, these covering arrays improve the size of the best-known covering arrays with the same parameters by almost 25 percent. The CA$(3q^4 -3; 4, \frac{q^2 +1}{2}, q)$ is used as the main ingredient in a recursive construction to obtain a CA$(5q^4 - 4q^3 - q^2 + 2q; 4, q^2 +1, q)$. Some improvements are obtained in the size of the best-known arrays using these covering arrays.
item.dc:creator: Kianoosh Shokri, Lucia Moura, Brett Stevens

item.title: On the quotient matrix and its distinct eigenvalues
item.description: arXiv:2604.03194v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $M$ be an $n\times n$ matrix partitioned into blocks according to a partition $P=\{C_{1},\dots,C_{\ell}\}$ of its index set, and let $Q$ be the corresponding equitable quotient. We study when $Q$ contains every distinct eigenvalue of $M$, so that the distinct spectral data of a large structured matrix can be recovered from a lower-order quotient. We first correct the distinction between a coarsest equitable partition and a minimum-order quotient that captures all distinct eigenvalues. We then establish an exact block-lifting construction with characteristic polynomial $\chi_M(x)=\chi_Q(x)\prod_i(x-\theta_i)^{|C_i|-1}$, derive multiplicity-design consequences, and give a necessary and sufficient eigenspace criterion for quotient capture. Further results quantify automatic capture through geometric multiplicity and describe exact spectral factors generated by twin cells in graph matrices. Applications to adjacency, weighted adjacency, Laplacian, signless Laplacian, distance, and distance-based Laplacian matrices are validated, including minimal one-cell refinements that recover eigenvalues hidden by collapsed twin classes.
item.dc:creator: Bilal Ahmad Rather, Jianfeng Wang, Zhaoxi Li

item.title: Counting symmetric unimodular triangulations
item.description: arXiv:2605.14150v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The objects of study are triangulations of the dilated standard triangle in the plane. Motivated by work on T-curves (Geiselmann et al., 2026), the focus lies on unimodular triangulations with a fixed symmetry axis. Lower and upper bounds are given, in combination with full enumerations of a few small cases.
item.dc:creator: Kamillo Ferry, Michael Joswig, J\"org Rambau

item.title: Modular Constructions of g-Golomb Rulers
item.description: arXiv:2607.07931v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A set \(\mathcal{G}\) of integers is a \(g\)-Golomb ruler if each positive difference appears at most \(g\) times between any 2 elements of the set, and \(G(g,n)\) denotes the minimum diameter of such a ruler with \(n\) marks. We prove a general lemma for passing from certain modular constructions to ordinary \(g\)-Golomb rulers. The key point is that, in a modular \(g\)-Golomb ruler, no cyclic gap length can occur more than \(g\) times. This gives a larger guaranteed cut than the previous average gap argument. We apply this lemma to cyclic relative difference sets, Singer sets, Ruzsa--Spence rulers, and Paley quadratic residues to provide many competing constructions for \(g\)-Golomb Rulers. A computation on the grid \(1\le g\le500\), \(n=g+b\), \(2\le b\le500\), compares the four resulting construction families.
item.dc:creator: Aditya Gupta

item.title: Ideal G{\aa}rding polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2607.16832v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce ideal G{\aa}rding polynomials, a convexity-enhanced subclass of G\aa{}rding polynomials whose G{\aa}rding components are recursively convex under partial differentiation. This class strictly contains real stable polynomials and, after translation and homogenization, lies in the Lorentzian class. Our main result is that ideal G{\aa}rding polynomials still admit a robust structure theory despite this additional convexity: they are preserved under polarization, satisfy natural closure properties, and support a linear preserver theory. A key contribution of this paper is a universal model for univariate G{\aa}rding polynomials, described by monotone root sequences and equivalently by volume polynomials of Pitman--Stanley polytopes. We establish quotient concavity, and Newton--Maclaurin type inequalities, which leads to the polarization theorem, and suggests further connections with convex geometry and Lorentzian polynomials.
item.dc:creator: Hao Fang, Biao Ma

item.title: Proof of Barry's Four Hankel Determinant Conjectures
item.description: arXiv:2607.18644v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Barry introduced a central transform of integer sequences and proposed four conjectures concerning the Hankel transforms of central transform of four rational families. We prove these four conjectures. The proofs are unified within a common algebraic framework: we interpret the Hankel determinants as Gram determinants and use a basis of shifted monic Chebyshev polynomials to reveal the finite-band structure of the associated Gram matrices.
item.dc:creator: Feihu Liu, Ying Wang, Zihao Zhang

item.title: Weight-constrained cut-down de Bruijn sequences
item.description: arXiv:2607.22350v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In 2011/12, Ruskey, Sawada, Stevens and Williams showed that a binary cut-down de Bruijn sequence can be constructed containing all $n$-tuples of Hamming weight either $r$ or $r+1$ for every possible $r$, and no others. In this paper we examine extensions of this result that require choosing a weight-like function applying to $n$-tuples with symbols taken from an alphabet of arbitrary (finite) size. We consider three possible such weight functions, and in each case establish an analogous result to that of Ruskey et al.
item.dc:creator: Chris J Mitchell, Peter R Wild

item.title: Counterexamples to the Minimum Period Conjecture for Restricted Partition Functions
item.description: arXiv:2608.02085v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a finite sequence of positive integers $\boldsymbol{a}=(a_1,\dots,a_n)$, the restricted partition function $q_{\boldsymbol{a}}(k)$ denote the number of nonnegative integer solutions to the equation $a_1x_1+a_2x_2+\cdots +a_nx_n=k$. It is proved to be a quasi-polynomial of degree $n-1$. Write $q_{\boldsymbol{a}}(k)=\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}c_j(k)k^j$ with periodic coefficient functions $c_j$, and set $b_m=\#\{i:m\mid a_i\}$. In 2008, Beck, Sam, and Woods conjectured that the minimum period of $c_j(k)$ is $\mathrm{lcm}\{m:b_m>j\}$. In this paper, we derive an exact root-of-unity formula for every coefficient function $c_j(k)$. The formula proves the conjectured divisibility upper bound, but it also reveals a lower bound for the period of $c_j(k)$. Both divisibility bounds are sharp. This leads us to construct a family of counterexamples to this conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Feihu Liu, Jinlong Tang, Guoce Xin, Chen Zhang

item.title: Hankel Transform and $(\alpha,\beta)$ Somos-4 Sequences
item.description: arXiv:2608.08703v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An $(\alpha,\beta)$ Somos-$4$ sequence $S_n$ is defined by the recurrence $S_nS_{n-4}=\alpha S_{n-1}S_{n-3}+\beta S_{n-2}^2$ ($n\geq 4$), with suitable initial values, where $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are constant parameters. A widely studied question is the following: When does the Hankel transform of a generating function become an $(\alpha,\beta)$ Somos-4 sequence? In particular, how can $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be derived for such a function? A sufficient condition for this problem has been established by Wang and Zhang. In this paper, we obtain the following three main results. (i): We extend the Wang--Zhang sufficient condition by working over the rational function field. Then we combine this result with the Sulanke--Xin quadratic transformation to resolve all of Barry's currently unsolved $(\alpha,\beta)$ Somos-4 conjectures, which arise in diverse contexts, including generalized Catalan recurrences, Riordan arrays, generalized Bernstein arrays, and elliptic curves. (ii): We show that the odd and even subsequences of an $(\alpha,\beta)$ Somos-4 sequence are again $(\alpha,\beta)$ Somos-4 sequences with transformed parameters. This is employed to establish Barry's Hurwitz transform conjecture. (iii): Using the theory of orthogonal polynomials, we prove a Hankel determinant formula and thereby prove a conjecture related to the $(\alpha,\beta)$ Somos-4 sequence. In addition, we prove some conjectures on formulas for periodic Hankel determinants.
item.dc:creator: Feihu Liu, Ying Wang, Zihao Zhang

item.title: A polynomial time algorithm for almost bounded denumerant
item.description: arXiv:2608.14985v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Sylvester's denumerant $d(t; \boldsymbol{A})$ counts the number of nonnegative integer solutions to $\sum_{i=1}^{N} a_i x_i = t$, where $\boldsymbol{A} = (a_1, \dots, a_N)$ is a sequence of positive integers with $\gcd(\boldsymbol{A}) = 1$. In 2025, Xin and Zhang gave a polynomial time algorithm in $N$ for computing $d(t; \boldsymbol{A})$ when the entries of $\boldsymbol{A}$ are bounded by a constant. In this paper, we extend this algorithm by incorporating Barvinok's algorithm, enabling it to handle the case where a fixed number of entries of $\boldsymbol{A}$ are allowed to be unbounded.
item.dc:creator: Guoce Xin, Chen Zhang, Zihao Zhang

item.title: Taylor Positivity of Ehrhart Polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2609.03327v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $P$ be a $d$-dimensional lattice polytope with Ehrhart polynomial $L_P(t)$. Motivated by the study of Ehrhart positivity and magic positivity, we investigate the Taylor coefficients $\mathsf{A}_j(P;k)$ in the shifted expansion $L_P(t)=\sum_{j=0}^{d}\mathsf{A}_j(P;k)(t-k)^j$ about a real center $k$. In this paper, we obtain the following four main results. (i) We give exact formulas for these coefficients in terms of the ordinary Ehrhart coefficients, the $h^*$-vector, elementary symmetric functions, and Stirling numbers. (ii) We denote by $\tau(P)$ and $\tau^+(P)$ the smallest nonnegative integral centers at which all Taylor coefficients are nonnegative and positive, respectively. If $s$ is the degree of the $h^*$-polynomial, then $0\leq\tau(P)\leq\tau^+(P)\leq\min\{\max\{0,s-1\},\lfloor\frac{d-1}{2}\rfloor\}$. As an application, we slightly improve an upper bound due to Beck, De Loera, Develin, Pfeifle, and Stanley. That is, every real root of $L_P(t)$ lies in $[-d,\lfloor\frac{d-1}{2}\rfloor)$. (iii) Let $\rho(P)$ be the smallest nonnegative real center such that the Taylor coefficients are nonnegative. If $\lambda_{\mathbb{R}}(f)$ denotes the largest real zero of $f(t)$, with value $-\infty$ when no such zero exists, then $\rho(P)=\max\{0,\max_{0\leq j<d}\lambda_{\mathbb{R}}\!(L_P^{(j)})\}$. (iv) We establish structural properties of the Taylor coefficients $\mathsf{A}_j(P;k)$, including derivative interlacing, palindromic reflection symmetries, and Laguerre and Newton inequalities. As a final note, these results provide a systematic partial answer to an open problem listed on the website of the American Institute of Mathematics.
item.dc:creator: Feihu Liu, Zihao Zhang

item.title: Real-Rootedness and Gamma-Positivity for a Variation of the Morris Constant Term
item.description: arXiv:2609.15201v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Beck and Pixton expressed the Ehrhart polynomial of the Birkhoff polytope as a weighted sum of constant terms of several multivariate rational functions. Xin and Zhang studied a class of constant terms $h_n(t)$, which can be regarded as a variation of the Morris constant term. They proved that $h_n(t)$ is a polynomial of degree $(n-1)^2$ and obtained many nice properties involving the Morris constant term identity. Let $h_n^*(y)=(1-y)^{(n-1)^2+1}\sum_{t\geq0}h_n(t)y^t$. For fixed $n\geq 3$, we obtain the following results for $h_n^*(y)$: (i): $h_n^*(y)$ is a polynomial with positive integer coefficients. (ii): $h_n^*(y)$ is real-rooted. In particular, all its roots are non-positive real numbers. (iii): $h_n^*(y)$ is Gamma-positive. Furthermore, $h_n^*(y)$ is palindromic, unimodal, and ultra log-concave. This confirms Xin and Zhang's conjecture regarding $h_n^*(y)$. In order to resolve this conjecture, we also developed an operator on the space of symmetric polynomials that preserves real stability. As a byproduct, we prove that every root of a Gamma polynomial associated with $h_n^*(y)$ is a negative real number.
item.dc:creator: Feihu Liu, Zihao Zhang

item.title: Counterexamples and symmetry for uneven orthogonal mass partitions in the plane
item.description: arXiv:2609.16757v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Gr\"unbaum asked whether every planar convex body admits, for every $0\leq t\leq 1/4$, two orthogonal lines cutting it into pieces with cyclically ordered areas $t,t,1/2-t,1/2-t$. B\'ar\'any posed the analogous question for well-behaved planar measures and conjectured that the answer there is negative. We confirm B\'ar\'any's conjecture in a particularly robust form: for every fixed $0<t<1/4$ we construct smooth, strictly positive, centrally symmetric, strongly log-concave measures arbitrarily close to the standard Gaussian for which the prescribed partition does not exist. In contrast, we prove that the partition exists for every $t$ whenever the measure is invariant under an orientation-reversing affine involution. We also exhibit a $96$-point counterexample for which no pair of perpendicular lines produces cyclic counts $8,8,40,40$.
item.dc:creator: Leonardo Mart\'inez-Sandoval

item.title: Unimodality for IDP Lattice Simplices of Prime Normalized Volume
item.description: arXiv:2609.19637v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recently, Ferroni constructed a family of counterexamples to the well-known conjecture in Ehrhart theory stating that the $h^*$-polynomial of a lattice polytope with the integer decomposition property is unimodal. This raises the question of whether the $h^*$-polynomial of a lattice simplex with the integer decomposition property remains unimodal. In this note, we prove that every lattice simplex with the integer decomposition property and prime normalized volume has a unimodal $h^*$-polynomial. Furthermore, we establish several sufficient conditions for the unimodality of the $h^*$-polynomial of such simplices.
item.dc:creator: Feihu Liu, Zihao Zhang

item.title: Counterexamples to the Mu--Welker recursive decomposition in every degree
item.description: arXiv:2609.23694v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The well-known open problem of Bell and Skandera asks whether a real-rooted polynomial $f(t)$ with positive integer coefficients and constant term one is the $f$-polynomial of a simplicial complex. Mu and Welker proved that if the recursive decomposition $f(t)=g(t)+th(t)$ satisfies the corresponding coefficient inequality $h_i<g_i$, then this open problem has an affirmative answer. Mu and Welker also conjectured that the real-rootedness of $f(t)$ implies that of $g(t)$ and $h(t)$. We give counterexamples to the conjecture of Mu and Welker for every degree at least three, and prove that the assertion holds in degrees $1$ and $2$. Moreover, each polynomial we construct is the $f$-polynomial of a simplicial complex.
item.dc:creator: Feihu Liu, Ying Wang, Zihao Zhang

item.title: $q$-Zeta positivity for root and Ferrers-cell posets
item.description: arXiv:2609.24541v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that Chapoton's $q$-Zeta numerator has nonnegative coefficients for the positive-root poset of every finite reduced irreducible crystallographic root system, graded by root height minus one and normalized by Chapoton's prescribed denominator. The same holds for every interval of the root poset with zero adjoined. The key observation is that adjoining a minimum changes the numerator only by the substitution $t\mapsto qt$. The numerator thereby becomes a nonnegative combination of flag $h$-numbers of a lower-semimodular lattice, and a classical labelling of the dual lattice gives a positive descent expansion. To make the coefficients explicit, we construct signed edge-lexicographic (EL) labellings of Ferrers-cell posets with nonincreasing boundaries. They give ballot-word formulas in types $A$, $B$, and $C$, which prove an observation of Chapoton in type $B$, and a coloured path formula in type $D$. For trapezoidal boundaries, one-boundary major-index enumerators evaluate the path sums in Gaussian-binomial form.
item.dc:creator: Qihang Wang, Weiye Li

item.title: Linearity bounds for APN functions
item.description: arXiv:2609.35689v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For $n\ge5$, let $F\colon\mathbb{F}_2^n\to \mathbb{F}_2^n$ be almost perfect nonlinear and write $N=2^n$. It is proven that the linearity $\mathcal{L}(F)$ of $F$, i.e., the largest absolute Walsh coefficient of a nonzero component, is at most $N-6$. If $n$ is even, it is further proven that $\mathcal{L}(F)\le N-\sqrt N/4-2$. These bounds improve the general upper bound of $N-4$ in odd dimension and $N-6$ in even dimensions $n \geq 10$. It is further proven that, for each fixed $k$, the $k$-th largest absolute Walsh coefficient among nonzero components, counted with multiplicity, is at most $(1+O_k(2^{-n}))N/\sqrt{k}$ as $n\to\infty$. The second and fourth largest coefficients are at most $2\lfloor N/3\rfloor$ and $N/2$, respectively. Finally, a bound on the linearity in terms of the number $q$ of nonplateaued nonzero components is derived. In odd dimension, for $q>0$, we have $\mathcal{L}(F)^2\le N(1+\sqrt{q(N-1)})$, so that $\mathcal{L}(F)/N\to1$ implies $q/N\to1$. In even dimension, for every $1/2\le C<1$, the condition $q\le(4C-C^2-1)N/4+1$ implies $\mathcal{L}(F)\le CN$. In particular, $q\le3N/16+2$ implies $\mathcal{L}(F)\le N/2$.
item.dc:creator: Christof Beierle, Lukas K\"olsch

item.title: Two families of Hermite normal form simplices
item.description: arXiv:2609.36818v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study Ehrhart coefficients, the integer decomposition property, and unimodular triangulations for two families of Hermite normal form simplices considered by Bruckamp, Caicedo, and Juhnke. The first family consists of simplices of the form $S_{\boldsymbol{a}}=\mathrm{conv}(0,e_1,\ldots,e_{d-1},\boldsymbol{a})$, where $\boldsymbol{a}=(a_1,\ldots,a_{d-1},N)$, and the second consists of the simplices $T_{d,N}=\mathrm{conv}\bigl(0,e_1,\ldots,e_{d-2},(d-2,\ldots,d-2,d-1,0),(1,\ldots,1,N)\bigr)$. For the family $T_{d,N}$, we prove unimodality of the Ehrhart coefficients in every dimension and determine the log-concave and real-rooted cases. For the subfamily $S_{\boldsymbol{a}}$ with $\boldsymbol{a}=(N-q,\ldots,N-q,N)$, we characterize both the integer decomposition property and the existence of a regular unimodular triangulation via a congruence condition on a negative continued fraction. We also give an arithmetic test for the integer decomposition property and finite triangulation tests for $S_{\boldsymbol{a}}$ with arbitrary $\boldsymbol{a}$. These results address three open questions of Bruckamp, Caicedo, and Juhnke.
item.dc:creator: Feihu Liu, Jinlong Tang, Sihao Tao, Zihao Zhang

item.title: Optimal discrepancy for triangles
item.description: arXiv:2610.00375v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that every $n$-point set in the plane has a two-coloring with discrepancy $O(n^{1/4})$ for all triangles. This improves the previous bound $O(n^{1/4}\sqrt{\log n})$ and matches the classical lower bound.
item.dc:creator: Gleb Smirnov

item.title: Upper $k$-Star-Forming Sets, $k$-Independence, and Upper Domination
