item.description: arXiv:2610.03785v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a positive integer $k$, let $\beta_k(G)$ be the maximum cardinality of a vertex set inducing maximum degree less than $k$, and let $SF_k(G)$ be the maximum cardinality of a minimal $k$-star-forming set. The known inequality $\beta_k(G)\le SF_k(G)$ suggests asking when equality holds. We place this question in the framework of upper domination: at $k=1$, $\beta_1(G)=\alpha(G)$ and $SF_1(G)=\Gamma(G)$, so the classical equality $\Gamma=\alpha$ on bipartite graphs is exactly the first member of the proposed hierarchy. We prove the equality for complete bipartite graphs for every $k$, obtaining \[ \beta_k(K_{a,b})=SF_k(K_{a,b})=\max\{a,b,2k-2\}\qquad(a,b\ge k), \] and record the elementary low-degree case $\Delta(G)<k$. For $k=2$ we derive certificate restrictions for minimal $2$-star-forming sets in bipartite graphs. For chain graphs we go further: we prove $\beta_2(G)=SF_2(G)$ and obtain an exact formula for their common value. The proof uses the nested-neighborhood structure together with a classification of witnesses to the indispensability of a high internal-degree vertex. We retain the equality problem for chain graphs as a conjecture only for $k\ge3$, and formulate the broader bipartite conjecture. We also determine the upper domination number of every rectangular grid and combine it with the known exact dissociation number to compare $\Gamma$, $\beta_2$, and $SF_2$. In particular, $\Gamma=\beta_2$ on every even-by-even rectangular grid, while $\beta_2\le SF_2$ always; this motivates a grid equality conjecture whose even-by-even case would yield a three-parameter identity.
item.dc:creator: Rafik Sahbi

item.title: Random independent sets in uncrowded hypergraphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.08707v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given any fixed integer $k \ge 2$ and sufficiently large $d$, we show that the largest possible fractional chromatic number of a $k$-uniform $d$-degenerate uncrowded hypergraph $H$ (i.e., with girth at least $5$) satisfies \[ \chi_f(H) = (1 + o_d(1)) \left((k-1)\,\frac{d}{\log d}\right)^{\frac{1}{k-1}}. \] In fact, we prove that this holds for $k$-uniform $d$-degenerate hypergraphs of girth at least $g$, for any given $g \ge 5$. As a corollary, we obtain improved bounds on the fractional chromatic number of $d$-degenerate linear hypergraphs. This work builds upon a recent result by Allen, Dhawan, and Noel, extending it from graphs to hypergraphs. In addition to overcoming the new difficulties that arise in the hypergraph setting, our approach yields a simpler proof even in the original graph case. Our proof of the upper bound uses a simpler iterative procedure for sampling independent sets. We also establish bounds for fractional colorings with local demands, a framework introduced by Kelly and Postle, verifying a recent conjecture of Yu and Zhang. As a consequence, we obtain a degree-sequence bound on the independence number of uncrowded hypergraphs with a leading constant matching the shattering threshold. For the matching lower bound, we use a hypergraph variant of the uniform attachment model and harmonic vertex weights to bound the fractional chromatic number via linear programming duality, then remove all short cycles by deleting vertices of negligible total weight. We also replace the Catalan-number argument used in the graph case with a matrix-norm estimate, simplifying the analysis.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Dhawan, Lina Li, Abhishek Methuku, Minh-Quan Vo, Kewen Yuan

item.title: Tweaking the constant in the Linear Hadwiger Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.10831v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Norin and Steiner recently proved the Linear Hadwiger Conjecture. That is, there is an absolute constant $C$ such that every graph $G$ satisfies $\chi(G)\leqslant C\,\text{had}(G)$, where $\chi(G)$ is the chromatic number and $\text{had}(G)$ is the Hadwiger number of $G$. They estimate that their proof gives a non-optimised constant $C$ of order $10^{100}$. This paper uses AI assistance to optimise their argument, and shows that every graph $G$ satisfies $\chi(G)\,\leqslant\,1{,}118{,}430\,\text{had}(G)$.
item.dc:creator: David R. Wood

item.title: Ehrhart positivity for paving positroids
item.description: arXiv:2610.21501v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A central conjecture of Ferroni, Jochemko, and Schr\"{o}ter posits that every positroid is Ehrhart positive. While Ehrhart positivity has recently been verified for notable classes such as lattice path matroids and series-parallel matroids, the general conjecture remains open. In this paper, we prove that the base polytope of any paving positroid has positive Ehrhart coefficients. This establishes a new class of Ehrhart positive positroids and provides substantial evidence supporting this conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Feihu Liu, Zihao Zhang

item.title: Extra-fine sheaves and interaction decompositions
item.description: arXiv:2009.12646v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce an original notion of (upper) extra-fine sheaf on a topological space, for which \v{C}ech cohomology in strictly positive degree vanishes. We apply this notion when the topological space is a partially ordered set (poset) equipped with the Alexandroff topology and the sheaves are made of duals of decomposable functors of vector spaces. The decomposition of the functor is known as interaction decomposition and can be expressed by a novel sum-intersection condition. We use these results to compute the dimension of the space of global sections when the sheaves are derived from those freely generated over a presheaf (of finite sets); this generalizes and makes topological classical counting formulae for the number of solutions of the linearized marginal problem (Kellerer and Mat\'u\v{s}). We finish with a comparison theorem between the \v{C}ech cohomology associated to a covering and the topos cohomology of the poset with coefficients in the presheaf, which is also the cohomology of a cosimplicial local system over the nerve of the poset. For that, we give a detailed treatment of cosimplicial local systems on simplicial sets. The appendixes present presheaves, sheaves relative \v{C}ech cohomology, and their application to the marginal problem.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Bennequin, Olivier Peltre, Gr\'egoire Sergeant-Perthuis, Juan Pablo Vigneaux

item.title: On the tangent bundle and the divisor theory of a general matroid
item.description: arXiv:2510.06609v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Extending classical algebro-geometric constructions to arbitrary matroids, we construct a $K$-class $T_M\in K(M)$ for every loopless matroid $M$. When $M$ is realizable by a linear subspace $L$, $T_M$ recovers the $K$-class of the tangent bundle of the wonderful compactification $W_L$. We derive two formulas for the total Chern class of $T_M$ (one combinatorial and one geometric) and show that the associated Todd class agrees with the Todd class appearing in the matroid Hirzebruch--Riemann--Roch formula. To develop a positivity theory entirely at the combinatorial level, we introduce the notion of a "fake effective cone", a combinatorial analogue of the classical effective cone, and use it to characterize big and nef divisors in $A(M)$. Finally, we define the $\beta_S$ classes, obtained from Cremona conjugates of the classical $\alpha_S$ classes, and study their properties to provide a rich and computable family of combinatorially nef divisors.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Int. Math. Res. Not. IMRN, 2026, no. 17, rnag188
item.dc:creator: Ronnie Cheng

item.title: A Complexity Dichotomy for Edge Subdivision to $H$-Free Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2604.24228v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For a fixed graph $H$, \HFS\ asks whether at most $k$ edge subdivisions can make an input graph contain no induced copy of $H$. We establish a complexity dichotomy for every fixed nonempty $H$: the problem is polynomial-time solvable if every component of $H$ is a subdivided star or a subdivided bistar and at most one component is a subdivided bistar; it is NP-complete otherwise. In every NP-complete case, the Exponential Time Hypothesis rules out a $2^{o(k)}n^{O(1)}$-time algorithm. For every fixed $H$, the problem admits a $2^{O(k)}n^{O(1)}$-time algorithm.
item.dc:creator: Marta Piecyk, R. B. Sandeep

item.title: An $\widetilde{O}(n^3)$-time FPRAS for the Permanent
item.description: arXiv:2609.20717v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give an FPRAS for the permanent of an $n\times n$ $0/1$ matrix with running time $\widetilde O(n^3)$. Our algorithm extends to a strongly polynomial FPRAS for arbitrary nonnegative matrices with the same running-time bound (but in the unit-cost arithmetic model). Jerrum, Sinclair, and Vigoda (2004) gave the first FPRAS for the permanent of a nonnegative matrix. The running time was subsequently improved to $\widetilde{O}(n^7)$ by Bez\'akov\'a, \v{S}tefankovi\v{c}, Vazirani, and Vigoda (2008), and recently to $\widetilde{O}(n^6)$ by Chen, Vigoda, and Yang (2026). We introduce a multicommodity-flow bound inspired by electrical flows, replacing the usual path-length factor by routing energy. For the classical JSV chain with perfect-matching weights multiplied by $n^2$, we prove a relaxation-time bound of $O(n^3\log n)$ and obtain comparable bounds for estimating the stationary probabilities of having a specified pair of unmatched vertices. We use a separate chain on assignments to generate a warm start at any given temperature, avoiding the long initialization of the JSV chain. Finally, we replace the JSV chain with a new chain that uses only $n$ hole weights and speeds up hole-weight learning by a factor of $n$.
item.dc:creator: Xiaoyu Chen, Heng Guo, Eric Vigoda, Xiongxin Yang

item.title: Euclidean Distance Optimization Within the Grassmannian
item.description: arXiv:2610.02018v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Given a subvariety of the Grassmannian and a data point, we seek to find a point on the subvariety minimizing the Euclidean distance to the data point. The number of complex critical points of this optimization problem is the Euclidean distance (ED) degree. We show that the ED discriminant of the whole Grassmannian, that is, the set of data points with a number of critical points different than the ED degree, is the discriminant of the characteristic polynomial of the data as a projection matrix. Another closely connected algebraic complexity measure for a subvariety in the Grassmannian is the Grassmann distance (GD) degree, which is the number of complex critical points of the distance optimization problem when the data point itself is in the Grassmannian. We give formulae for ED and GD degrees of geometrically meaningful subvarieties of the Grassmannian, namely, products of smaller Grassmannians, matroid realization varieties, and Schubert varieties.
item.dc:creator: Hannah Friedman, Serkan Ho\c{s}ten, Andrea Rosana

item.title: Equivariant Chow functions and Wonderful Models in type A and B
item.description: arXiv:2610.03138v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove a general inversion formula in the equivariant incidence algebras of geometric lattices that relates the equivariant Chow function with the equivariant super-reduced characteristic function. We apply this result to the case of minimal wonderful models for hyperplane arrangements associated to root systems, with the natural action of the corresponding Weyl group. Applying this formula to type $A$ (i.e. the partition lattices), we recover Getzler's compositional identity in type $A$. In type $B$ (i.e. the signed partition lattice), we recover Henderson's result, expressing the equivariant Chow generating series in terms of the same series in type $A$ and the equivariant characteristic generating series of type $B$. Moreover, we obtain a new compositional identity for the equivariant Chow generating series.
item.dc:creator: Roberto Pagaria, Tommaso Scognamiglio

item.title: Ehrhart Properties under Operations on Lattice Polytopes
item.description: arXiv:2610.06338v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper investigates the preservation of three classes of Ehrhart properties under various operations on lattice polytopes. These operations include Cartesian products, lattice joins, lattice pyramids, free sums, Minkowski sums, Cayley sums, reflexive polarity, and integral dilations. Specifically, we consider the following properties frequently studied in Ehrhart theory: (i): Positivity of Ehrhart coefficients, including Ehrhart positivity and magic positivity. In particular, we present lattice point counting formulas for the polytopes generated by these operations. (ii): Coefficient properties of the $h^*$-polynomial, including symmetry, unimodality, log-concavity, ultra log-concavity, real-rootedness, and $\gamma$-positivity. (iii): Geometric properties, including the spanning property, the integer decomposition property, very ampleness, and the existence of unimodular triangulation, regular unimodular triangulation, and quadratic triangulation. We determine which properties are preserved under these eight operations, establishing preservation theorems or constructing explicit counterexamples. Furthermore, when a property is not preserved in general, we investigate sufficient or equivalent conditions for its preservation.
item.dc:creator: Feihu Liu

item.title: A deterministic polynomial-time algorithm for the Bilu--Linial signing problem on bipartite graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.09972v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm for the Bilu--Linial signing problem on bipartite graphs. For every finite simple bipartite graph of maximum degree at most an integer $\Delta\ge3$, the algorithm assigns signs to its edges so that the signed adjacency matrix has operator norm strictly less than $2\sqrt{\Delta-1}$. Our algorithm builds on the randomized recursive repair framework of Jadbabaie, Saberi, and Sra~\cite{JSS26}, with deterministic rules for sign selection and vertex deletion.

item.title: Combinatorial bounds for the v-number of binomial edge ideals
item.description: arXiv:2610.18213v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the local $\mathrm v$-numbers of binomial edge ideals from a combinatorial perspective. For each minimal prime $P_{\mathcal S}$ of $J_G$, indexed by a cutset $\mathcal S$ of $G$, we consider two combinatorial invariants, $\mathrm v^-_{\mathcal S}(G)$ and $\mathrm v^+_{\mathcal S}(G)$, defined in terms of transversals of suitable hypergraphs, and show that the local $\mathrm v$-number $\mathrm v_{P_{\mathcal S}}(J_G)$ satisfies $\mathrm v^-_{\mathcal S}(G)\leq \mathrm v_{P_{\mathcal S}}(J_G)\leq \mathrm v^+_{\mathcal S}(G)$. Under a suitable hypothesis on the connected components, we provide explicit graph-theoretic descriptions of these invariants and analyze when they coincide, giving a combinatorial way to determine the local $\mathrm v$-numbers. As an application, we derive a sufficient condition for this coincidence, which applies to a broad class of graphs. Furthermore, we identify a constant that controls the gap between $\mathrm v^-_{\mathcal S}(G)$ and $\mathrm v^+_{\mathcal S}(G)$, thereby showing that the local $\mathrm{v}$-number lies within a bounded interval. Applications to cycles and trees illustrate both the equality criterion and the resulting bounds.

item.title: Enumerating Integral Points on Triangles in $\mathbb{R}^3$
item.description: arXiv:2610.20899v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present two ways of constructing Ehrhart polynomials corresponding to certain triangles in $\mathbb{R}^3$. One of our methods employs Popoviciu's Theorem, while the other method uses a version of Pick's Theorem adapted to rank-2 lattices in $\mathbb{R}^3$. We then apply our methods to linear Diophantine equations of the form $ax+by+cz=n$ and develop upper and lower bounds on the number of solutions in nonnegative integers $x$, $y$, and $z$. The bounds we develop are closed form quasi-polynomials, and the difference between them is bounded by a constant depending only on $a$ and $b$. As an application, we prove that the $k$th Frobenius number exists for any triple of positive integers and any $k$.
